small_path_half_up.equivalent_reason: equivalent: on an exact tie the half-up estimate is odd and the tie_odd correction restores RNE

recip_half_up.equivalent_reason: equivalent: 2^54 mod root == root/2 has no solution, so div_rne(2^54, root) never ties

exp_clip_1023.equivalent_reason: equivalent: exp_q15 is 0 for every index >= 710, so clipping at 1023 or 1024 reads 0

kv_bank_sel_undelayed.equivalent_reason: equivalent: raddr is written in SC_RD/AV_VRD and kvq_r is first consumed three states later (SC_DOT/AV_VISSUE), by which time raddr == raddr_d

no_div127_up_correction.equivalent_reason: equivalent: INV127_Q32 = 33818641 > 2^32/127, so the estimate never falls below the true quotient and the +1 branch is unreachable

cs_high_gap_one_cycle.equivalent_reason: equivalent ONLY under the assumption that the core clock is 50 MHz (20 ns period; the unit test uses exactly that, the board runs the core at 50 MHz): CS# then stays high one core cycle (20 ns) which already exceeds tCS(read) = 10 ns, so CS_HIGH=2 is only margin. At a core clock faster than 100 MHz (period < 10 ns) this fault WOULD violate tCS and the model TCS check would catch it; the e2e sim uses a time-scaled 2 ns clock with a scaled tCS of 1 ns and so stays equivalent there too

abort_leaves_nib_ph.equivalent_reason: equivalent: the S_GAP exit that starts the next command also clears nib_ph, and nibbles are only captured in S_RUN, so the stale value is never observed

cs_not_released_after_spi.equivalent_reason: equivalent at the pins: when the S transaction ends the pins go back to qspi_reader, whose CS# is high (idle: CS# rises there, 8 cycles late) or low (burst parked by backpressure: CS# stays low with SCLK low and no clocks). The CS# rise that latches WREN/WRDI/WRR is only deferred to the next CS# rise, which always comes before any further command byte is clocked: the next S frame forces CS# high first (S_PT_WAIT sets cs_n_q=1 before pt_active) and a decode seek raises it in qspi_reader. WEL/WIP are only observed through S frames or take effect before the next decode read, so the deferral is unobservable; the directed WREN/RDSR/WRDI/RDSR cases between decode steps (reader parked with CS# low) pass with the fault

reader_not_reset_by_watchdog.equivalent_reason: equivalent under every stimulus the simulation can create: the stall is injected on the byte stream (st_valid forced low), which does not hang the reader, and a freshly reset top_decode issues seek_req for its first read, which makes the reader abort whatever burst it was in (newer address wins, unit qspi tests) and drop its pending byte. The reader reset in the watchdog path is defence in depth against a reader hang; a hang inside the reader cannot be produced without editing the reader, whose own unit tests and faults cover its seek/abort handling

spi_takeover_without_settle_wait.equivalent_reason: equivalent: the 256-cycle wait only guards against taking the pins while the reader still clocks its last prefetched byte. The reader parks within about 16 cycles of the last byte top_decode accepts, which is before done; the host cannot send an S frame before it has received the 11-byte R response (11 x 10 bit times >= 880 cycles at 115200 baud, 880 cycles even at CPB=8 x 10 x 11) and the S header itself takes 3 more byte times, so the wait is always already elapsed in a protocol-conforming exchange. Removing it is unobservable
